The default session uses a tagged-JSON serializer in `src/tessel/`.

- **`SignedCookieSessionInterface`** (`src/tessel/sessions.py:284`) is the default session interface. Its `serializer` attribute (line 300) is `session_json_serializer`, an instance of `TypedCookieSerializer` (line 273). It passes that serializer to the signing serializer that handles the cookie (line 316).
- **`TypedCookieSerializer`** (`src/tessel/json/tag.py:219`) walks the session data. On dump, it asks each registered tag whether it applies to a value and, if so, wraps the value as a single-key dict such as `{" t": [...]}`. On load, it looks for those one-key dicts and reverses the conversion.
- **`TypeMarker`** (`src/tessel/json/tag.py:60`) is the base class for the tags. Each subclass implements `check`, `to_json` and `to_python`, and has a `key` that identifies it.
- **Tag subclasses** (same file):
  - `TagTuple` (line 133) handles tuples, stored as a list under `" t"`.
  - `TagBytes` (line 159) handles bytes, stored as base64 under `" b"`.
  - `TagDateTime` (line 205) handles datetimes, stored as an HTTP date string under `" d"`.
  - `TagDict` (line 93) escapes real dicts that happen to look like a tag, so they don't get misread on load.
  - `PassDict` and `PassList` pass dicts and lists through while the serializer recurses into their contents.
  - `TagMarkup` and `TagUUID` handle markup and UUID values.

I didn't open the file bodies, so the exact tag keys above come from my knowledge of this Flask-derived design, not from reading this repo. Also, `vendor/python/` holds many copies of the same package; the live one is `src/tessel`.
